March, 2025
Author: Manju Rani Chauhan

Bench: Manju Rani Chauhan
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

Case :- Application U/S 528 Bnss No. - 6919 of 2025

1.

Heard Mr. Krishna Kant Dubey, learned counsel for the applicants, Ms. Kirti Singh, learned Aga
for the State and perused the records.

2. Act, Police Station-Dankaur,
District-Gautam Buddha Nagar, pending before the court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate-I,
Gautam Buddha Nagar on the basis of compromise.

"The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed to quash the charge-sheet dated 10.11.2022, order dated 27.09.2024 and proceedings of Case No. 2226 of 2022 (State vs. Deepak Saxena and 5 others) arising out of Case Crime No. 314 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 IPC & Section 3/4 DP Act, Police Station-Dankaur,
District-Gautam Buddha Nagar, on the basis of compromise, pending in the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate-1, Gautam Buddha Nagar.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: By order 02.12.2024, this Court had directed the parties to appear before the court concerned along with application as well as compromise deed for verification of the compromise.

The order dated 02.12.2024 is being reproduced herein below:
"Mr. Kunal Singh, Advocate holding brief of Mr. Krishna Kant Dubey, learned counsel for the applicants is permitted to carry out necessary amendment during course of the day praying for setting aside the order dated 27.09.2024.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants and learned A.G.A. for the State.

The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed to quash the charge sheet dated 10.11.2022 and order dated 27.09.2024 as well as the entire proceeding of Case No.2226 of 2022 (State vs. Deepak Saxena and 5 Others), arising out of Case Crime No.0314 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act,
Police Station-Dankaur, District-Gautam Buddha Nagar, pending before the court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate-I, Gautam Buddha Nagar on the basis of compromise.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate-I, Gautam Buddha Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the present dispute is a result of matrimonial discord between the applicant no.1 (husband) and opposite party no.2.
Now, the parties have reconciled their differences and a compromise has been entered between them and they are decided to live separately.
In this regard, a compromise deed on behalf of both the parties has been filed before the court concerned, copy of the same has been appended as Annexure No.3 of this application.
Therefore, continuance of proceedings against the applicants would futile exercise and wastage of time of the Court and will be abuse of process of law.

Hence,
proceedings of the aforesaid case be quashed in the light of law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Gian Singh v. State of Punjab reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303.

entities.text: Gian Singh v. State of Punjab reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned AGA, however, submits that it is the concerned court below, which has to verify the fact as to whether the parties have entered into compromise, hence the applicants may approach the concerned court below and move an application with respect to compromise between the parties, which will be decided in accordance with law.

Deepak Saxena And 5 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 4 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84832144/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above, both the parties are directed to appear before the court below along with an application for verification of compromise deed as well as a certified copy of this order.

It is expected that the trial court may fix a date for the verification of the compromise and after ensuring the presence of parties, pass an appropriate order with respect to the same in accordance with law, as expeditiously as possible,
preferably within a period of two months from today.

While passing the order verifying the compromise, the concerned court shall also record the statement of the parties as to whether all the terms and conditions mentioned in the original compromise deed, so filed, have been fulfilled or not?
Upon due verification of compromise, the court below may pass appropriate order in that regard and send a report to this Court.
Put up this case on 06.01.2025, as fresh.
Till then, no coercive measure shall be taken against the applicants in the aforesaid case."
In compliance of the aforesaid order, a report from the ACJM-I, Gautam Buddha Nagar is placed on the record as is evident from the office report dated 04.02.2025.
As per the report dated 01.02.2025 the parties did not appear before the court concerned for verification of compromise.
Heard Mr. Srinath Mishra, learned Advocate holding brief of Sri Santosh Kumar Dubey, counsel for the applicants, Ms. Kirti Singh, learned AGA for the State, and perused the record.

Having heard submissions of learned counsel for the applicants and perusal of the record, this Court finds that no useful purpose would be served in keeping this petition pending, thus, the same is being decided at this stage in terms of Rules of the Court.
In view of the above, both the parties are directed to appear before the court below along with a certified copy of this order and permitted to file a proper compromise deed.

It is expected that the trial court may fix a date for the verification of the compromise and after ensuring the presence of parties, pass an appropriate order with respect to the same in accordance with law, as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of two months from today.

While passing the order verifying the compromise, the concerned court shall also record the statement of the parties as to whether all the terms and conditions mentioned in the original compromise deed, so filed, have been fulfilled or not.

The court in that scenario will allow the parties to obtain certified copy of the order verifying the compromise deed and it will be open to the applicants to approach this Court again for quashing of the proceedings.

Till verification of compromise between the parties by the court concerned or for a period of two months, whichever is earlier, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicants in the aforesaid Deepak Saxena And 5 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 4 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84832144/
3 case.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
With the aforesaid directions, this application is finally disposed of."
4.

In compliance of the aforesaid order, the compromise between the parties has been verified by First Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Gautam Buddha Nagar vide order dated 05.02.2025 in the presence of the parties alongwith their respective counsels.

entities.text: First Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Gautam Buddha Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: A certified copy of the order dated 05.02.2025 has been annexed as Annexure No.3 to this application affidavit.

5. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that on account of compromise entered into between the parties concerned, all disputes between them have come to an end, and therefore, further proceedings against the applicant in the aforesaid case is liable to be quashed by this Court.

6. Learned A.G.A. for the State do not dispute the aforesaid fact and submitted at the Bar that since the parties concerned have settled their dispute as mentioned above, therefore, they have no objection in quashing the impugned criminal proceedings against the applicants.

7. Before proceeding any further it shall be apt to make a brief reference to the following cases:-
i. B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and Another; (2003)4 SCC 675, ii. Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation; (2008) 9 SCC 677, iii. Manoj Sharma Vs. State and Others; (2008) 16 SCC 1, iv. Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab; (2012); 10 SCC 303, v. Narindra Singh and others Vs. State of Punjab; ( 2014) 6 SCC 466,
8.

Reference may also be made to the decision given by this Court in Shaifullah and Others Vs. State of U.P. &
Another; 2013 (83) ACC 278.

9. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, as noted herein above, and also the submissions made by the counsel for the parties, the court is of the considered opinion that no useful purpose shall be served by prolonging the proceedings of the above mentioned criminal case as the parties have already settled their dispute.

10. Act, Police Station-Dankaur, District-Gautam Buddha Nagar
